*"The giants of the molecular world"*

::: {.callout-note}
## Key Revelation
From simple building blocks, enormous structures emerge. Proteins fold, DNA encodes, and polymers give materials their properties. Life is macromolecular.
:::

## Proteins

Chains of amino acids that do everything in life.

### Amino Acids

20 standard amino acids, each with:
- Amino group ($-\text{NH}_2$)
- Carboxyl group (-COOH)
- R group (side chain: what makes each unique)

The general structure: $\text{H}_2\text{N}$-CH(R)-COOH, where R is the side chain unique to each amino acid.

### Peptide Bonds

Amino acids link by condensation, releasing water and forming the peptide bond (-CO-NH-) that chains amino acids together into proteins.

### Protein Structure

| Level | Description | Forces |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| Primary | Amino acid sequence | Covalent (peptide bonds) |
| Secondary | α-helix, β-sheet | Hydrogen bonds |
| Tertiary | 3D folding | All forces |
| Quaternary | Multiple chains | All forces |

### Protein Functions

- **Enzymes**: Catalyze reactions
- **Structural**: Collagen, keratin
- **Transport**: Hemoglobin
- **Immune**: Antibodies
- **Signaling**: Hormones

## Nucleic Acids

Information storage molecules.

### DNA Structure

![DNA double helix structure with sugar-phosphate backbone and base pairing.](../../media/images/fig-dna-helix.png){#fig-dna-helix}

Two antiparallel sugar-phosphate backbones connected by base pairs:
- **A-T**: Adenine pairs with thymine via 2 hydrogen bonds
- **G-C**: Guanine pairs with cytosine via 3 hydrogen bonds

### Double Helix

- 10 base pairs per turn
- 3.4 nm pitch
- Major and minor grooves
- Antiparallel strands

### RNA

- Single-stranded (usually)
- Uracil instead of thymine
- Sugar is ribose (not deoxyribose)
- Types: mRNA, tRNA, rRNA

## Polymers

Long chains of repeating units (monomers).

### Addition Polymers

Monomers add without losing atoms:

| Monomer | Polymer | Use |
|---------|---------|-----|
| Ethylene | Polyethylene | Plastic bags |
| Propylene | Polypropylene | Containers |
| Styrene | Polystyrene | Foam, packaging |
| Vinyl chloride | PVC | Pipes |

Example: n($\text{CH}_2\text{=CH}_2$) $\to$ $-[-\text{CH}_2\text{-CH}_2-]_n-$ (polyethylene)

### Condensation Polymers

Monomers lose small molecule (usually water):

| Type | Example | Use |
|------|---------|-----|
| Polyester | PET | Bottles, fabric |
| Polyamide | Nylon | Fibers, fabric |
| Polyurethane | PU | Foam, coatings |

## Carbohydrates

Sugars and their polymers.

### Monosaccharides

Simple sugars: glucose, fructose, galactose (all $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$)

### Disaccharides

Two sugars linked:
- Sucrose = glucose + fructose
- Lactose = glucose + galactose
- Maltose = glucose + glucose

### Polysaccharides

| Name | Function | Source |
|------|----------|--------|
| Starch | Energy storage | Plants |
| Glycogen | Energy storage | Animals |
| Cellulose | Structure | Plant cell walls |
| Chitin | Structure | Fungi, arthropods |

## Lipids

Not true polymers, but complex molecules.

### Fatty Acids

Long hydrocarbon chain + carboxyl group: $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_n\text{COOH}$

- **Saturated**: No double bonds, solid at room temperature
- **Unsaturated**: Double bonds, liquid at room temperature

### Phospholipids

Basis of cell membranes:

![Phospholipid structure: hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails.](../../media/images/fig-lipid-bilayer.png){#fig-phospholipid}

Each phospholipid has a hydrophilic head (phosphate group) and hydrophobic tails (fatty acid chains). In water, they spontaneously form bilayers with heads facing outward and tails facing inward.

## Experiments

### Protein Folding
Watch a chain of amino acids fold into its final structure.

### DNA Replication
Observe the double helix unzip and copy.

### Polymer Synthesis
Build polymers from monomers. Compare properties.

## Concepts

- **protein**: Amino acid polymer with complex structure
- **nucleic-acid**: Information-carrying polymer (DNA, RNA)
- **polymer**: Long chain of repeating units
- **carbohydrate**: Sugar or sugar polymer
